title: Sneaker Customizer with Save/Load State
prompt:
Create a single HTML file implementing a 3D sneaker/product customizer using Three.js. Since we don't have an actual sneaker model, load the provided 'robot.glb' model using GLTFLoader as a stand-in product to customize.

SCENE SETUP:
- Initialize a Three.js scene with a white/light gray background (color 0xf0f0f0).
- Add a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera rotation (enable damping).
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.6) and a directional light at (5, 10, 7) with intensity 1.0 and shadow enabled.
- Add a circular ground plane (radius 3, color 0xcccccc) at y=0 receiving shadows.
- Load 'robot.glb' using GLTFLoader, center it on the ground plane, scale it so it fits roughly within a 2-unit bounding box. Enable castShadow on all meshes.

CUSTOMIZATION SYSTEM:
The robot model has multiple mesh parts. Identify and store references to at least 3 distinct mesh children (or groups). Label them as 'partA', 'partB', 'partC' in the state. Each part can be customized:

1. COLOR: Each part has an independent color. Default all parts to their original material color. Provide a color palette with 6 preset colors: Red(0xff0000), Blue(0x0000ff), Green(0x00ff00), Yellow(0xffff00), Purple(0x800080), White(0xffffff).

2. MATERIAL TYPE: Each part can switch between 'standard', 'metallic', and 'glossy' materials:
   - 'standard': MeshStandardMaterial roughness=0.7, metalness=0.1
   - 'metallic': MeshStandardMaterial roughness=0.2, metalness=0.9
   - 'glossy': MeshStandardMaterial roughness=0.05, metalness=0.3

3. SCALE: Each part can be scaled independently from 0.5 to 2.0 (default 1.0).

UI PANEL (DOM elements on left side):
- A panel div (id='customizer-panel') with width 280px, positioned absolute left.
- Part selector: 3 buttons with ids 'btn-partA', 'btn-partB', 'btn-partC'. The selected part button should have class 'active' and a highlighted border.
- Color swatches: 6 clickable divs with class 'color-swatch' and data-color attribute. Ids: 'swatch-red','swatch-blue','swatch-green','swatch-yellow','swatch-purple','swatch-white'.
- Material selector: 3 buttons with ids 'btn-mat-standard', 'btn-mat-metallic', 'btn-mat-glossy'. Active one gets class 'active'.
- Scale slider: input range (id='scale-slider') min=0.5, max=2.0, step=0.1, default 1.0. Display current value in a span (id='scale-value').
- SAVE button (id='btn-save'): Saves entire customization state to localStorage key 'sneaker_config'.
- LOAD button (id='btn-load'): Loads from localStorage and applies all saved customizations.
- RESET button (id='btn-reset'): Resets all parts to default (original colors, 'standard' material, scale 1.0).
- A status text (id='status-text') that shows 'Saved!', 'Loaded!', or 'Reset!' for 2 seconds after respective actions.

ROTATION FEATURE:
- Press 'R' key to toggle auto-rotation of the model (rotate around Y axis at 0.01 rad/frame). Default: off.
- The rotation state should be tracked.

STATE MANAGEMENT - Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
{
  modelLoaded: boolean,
  selectedPart: 'partA'|'partB'|'partC',
  partColors: { partA: hexInt, partB: hexInt, partC: hexInt },
  partMaterials: { partA: 'standard'|'metallic'|'glossy', partB: ..., partC: ... },
  partScales: { partA: number, partB: number, partC: number },
  autoRotate: boolean,
  saveCount: number (increments each save),
  loadCount: number (increments each load),
  resetCount: number (increments each reset),
  statusText: string (current status message),
  cameraDistance: number (distance from camera to origin, updated each frame),
  frameCount: number (incremented each animation frame)
}

Ensure all state values are kept in sync with the actual 3D scene. When a color is applied, the mesh material color must change AND partColors must update. Same for materials and scales.

IMPORTANT: The animation loop must continuously update cameraDistance and frameCount. All NaN checks should pass - no values should ever be NaN.
physics_constraints: No physics simulation required. Scale values must be clamped between 0.5 and 2.0. Camera distance must always be a positive finite number. Auto-rotation speed is exactly 0.01 radians per frame when enabled.
